newsitem.title: USA: Calif. sues former owner of Golden Eagle Insurance.
newsitem.headline: Calif. sues former owner of Golden Eagle Insurance.

text.p: California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush said on Friday he filed a lawsuit against former Golden Eagle Insurance Co owner John Mabee, demanding the return of $69 million he allegedly owes the company.

Mabee, the former chairman of the board of privately-held Golden Eagle Insurance, was sued by Quackenbush for repayment of the $69 million in promissory notes allegedly owed to Golden Eagle through its affiliate Mesa Reinsurance Co.
The lawsuit, filed in San Francisco Superior Court, also seeks damages for allegedly fraudulent conduct by Mabee in operating Golden Eagle and Mesa Re, Quackenbush said.
"Mr. Mabee has not met my demand to return the $69 million, so a lawsuit is necessary to obtain the missing millions," Quackenbush said.
In January, Quackenbush served a court order to take over control of San Diego-based Golden Eagle Insurance, one of the largest writers of workers' compensation insurance in the state.
